passages.original: ad hominem dei sciscitandum mittit de futuris, et eum ad cuius hominem mittit despuit et facit in contumeliam maiestatis eius uitulas et has adorare secum facit populum. haec egit, et tamen non ilico est extinctus, sed diu in regno superfuit. et tu dicis: si fuissem haereticus, si, ut dicunt Lucifer, Pancratius et Hilarius, dei inpugnarem religionem, iam in me fuisset uindicatum. accipe adhuc quid huic contigerit Hieroboam regi, et tamen quomodo nec sic conuertatur ad deum, sed magis in suo perseuerans mortuus fuerit scelere, in suo defecerit sacrilegio: et fecit Hieroboam diem festum in mense octauo in die festo quinto decimo mensis secundum diem festum Iuda, et ascendit in sacrificium quod fecit in Bethel, ut sacrificarent uitulis quas fecit, et constituit in Bethel sacerdotes excelsorum quos fecit, et ascendit in sacrarium quod fecit in quinto decimo die mense octauo in die festo quem finxit a corde suo, et fecit diem festum filiis Israel et ascendit in sacrarium ut sacrificaret.
passages.english: He sends to the man of God to inquire about the future, and he spurns the one to whose man he sends, and in insult to his majesty he makes heifers and makes the people worship them together with him. These things he did, and yet he was not destroyed on the spot, but survived long in his kingdom. And you say: "If I had been a heretic, if, as Lucifer, Pancratius and Hilary say, I were attacking the religion of God, vengeance would already have been taken on me." Hear further what befell this king Jeroboam, and yet how not even so was he turned to God, but rather, persisting in his crime, he died, and perished in his sacrilege: "And Jeroboam made a feast day in the eighth month, on the fifteenth festal day of the month, after the manner of the feast day of Judah, and he went up to the sacrifice which he made in Bethel, that they might sacrifice to the heifers which he had made; and he appointed in Bethel priests of the high places which he had made; and he went up to the sanctuary which he had made, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, on the feast day which he had devised from his own heart; and he made a feast day for the children of Israel and went up to the sanctuary to sacrifice."
passages.notes: Lucifer of Cagliari is addressing the emperor (Constantius II); "Pancratius" is presumably Pancratius, a priest/legate associated with Lucifer and Hilary (of Poitiers or the Roman deacon Hilary); identification uncertain. "uitulas" (heifers) renders the Latin Bible's form for Jeroboam's golden calves. The quotation is 1 Kings (3 Kings) 12:32–33 in an Old Latin version.

passages.original: et tu es iniquus, qui, cum sis derelictus pro blasphemiis tuis a deo, tamen cum adulatoribus tuis quodcumque delinquis non reprehendatur, sed magis dicatur bene te agere. cum dicis: bene feci ad Alexandriam mittere militem ad auferendum Athanasium, et illi rectissime dicunt: tu cui conparandus eris, nisi illi qui per psalmographum notatur a spiritu sancto, quod enim, cum gerat iniqua, cum sit pessimus et execrabilis, tamen cupiens sit laudari ? dicis: nisi bene agerem, non adhuc mihi pepercisset deus;
passages.english: And you are the wicked one who, though you have been abandoned by God for your blasphemies, yet, with your flatterers, whatever wrong you commit is not rebuked, but rather it is said that you are acting well. When you say, "I did well to send a soldier to Alexandria to remove Athanasius," and they say, "Quite rightly," to whom will you be compared, if not to the one who is marked out by the Holy Spirit through the psalmist, namely that, though he does wicked things, though he is most evil and accursed, yet he desires to be praised? You say: "If I were not acting well, God would not have spared me until now";
passages.notes: The sentence beginning "to whom will you be compared" is loosely constructed in the Latin ("quod enim..."); rendered according to evident sense. The psalm allusion is to Psalm 9/10 (the sinner praised in the desires of his soul), cited in the preceding context.
